title: Tricocare PH1 Exam Day 1-4
content:
Tricocare PH1 – Comprehensive Multiple Choice Exam

Answer all 20 questions. Circle the BEST answer for each. This paper covers content from Days 1 to 4.

1. Which of the following best explains why clients often ask stylists about scalp issues?

A. Stylists are medically trained to treat scalp disorders

B. Salons are more accessible than clinics

C. Hairdressers see the scalp more frequently than GPs

D. Clients trust stylists' product recommendations more than doctors'



2. What is the function of the dermal papilla within the hair follicle?

A. It produces sebum to coat the hair

B. It provides blood supply to support hair growth

C. It controls melanin production in the medulla

D. It anchors the follicle in the hypodermis



3. Which component of the hair strand contributes most to strength and elasticity?

A. Medulla

B. Pigment granules

C. Cortex

D. Cuticle



4. Which of the following would most likely disrupt the scalp microbiome?

A. Mild herbal shampoos

B. Regular brushing

C. Overuse of harsh chemical products

D. Warm water rinses



5. What is the typical duration of the anagen phase for scalp hair?

A. 2–3 weeks

B. 2–7 years

C. 1–2 months

D. 10–15 days



6. What makes Type 4 hair particularly prone to breakage?

A. Low density

B. Oval follicle shape

C. High elasticity

D. Tight curl pattern with fewer cuticle layers



7. Which statement is TRUE about follicle miniaturisation?

A. It results in stronger, thicker hairs

B. It is always caused by trauma

C. It leads to shorter, finer regrowth

D. It permanently damages the cortex





8. What does high hair porosity usually indicate?

A. Cuticles are tightly sealed

B. Hair holds moisture for long periods

C. Cuticles are lifted or damaged

D. The medulla is overactive



9. Which condition is associated with autoimmune causes and patchy hair loss?

A. Traction Alopecia

B. Alopecia Areata

C. Folliculitis

D. Tinea Capitis



10. Why should stylists avoid diagnosing scalp conditions?

A. It's unnecessary; most conditions resolve on their own

B. It could delay the client receiving proper medical care

C. Clients prefer home remedies

D. Insurance covers stylist diagnoses



11. Salicylic acid is classified as which type of compound?

A. Alpha hydroxy acid

B. Protein bond relaxer

C. Beta hydroxy acid

D. Emollient oil





12. What is the role of caffeine in scalp treatments?

A. Acts as a cleansing surfactant

B. Enhances elasticity of the cortex

C. Stimulates circulation to the follicle

D. Blocks hormone-related hair loss



13. Which ingredient is best known for barrier support and reducing inflammation?

A. Shea butter

B. Castor oil

C. Niacinamide

D. Sulphur



14. Which of the following is NOT a contraindication for scalp therapy?

A. Infected lesions

B. Scalp psoriasis flare-up

C. Recent open wound

D. Healthy dandruff-free scalp



15. What distinguishes seborrheic dermatitis from simple dandruff?

A. Seborrheic dermatitis causes less irritation

B. Dandruff flakes are red and greasy

C. Seborrheic dermatitis includes redness and greasy yellow flakes

D. Dandruff is contagious



16. Which practice can help maintain a healthy scalp microbiome?

A. Frequent bleaching

B. Avoiding all hair products

C. Using pH-balanced cleansers

D. Exfoliating daily



17. What is the safest way to approach a suspected scalp infection in a client?

A. Recommend antifungal shampoo immediately

B. Provide a deep cleansing mask

C. Refer them to a medical professional promptly

D. Continue treatment with gloves on



18. Why is massage included in scalp care treatments?

A. It removes toxins from the bloodstream

B. It stimulates nerves in the medulla

C. It promotes relaxation and circulation to the follicle

D. It closes open pores after exfoliation



19. What is the correct legal language to use when advising a client about a scalp concern?

A. 'I think you have eczema'

B. 'Let me diagnose that for you'

C. 'I recommend seeing a specialist about this'

D. 'You have psoriasis for sure'

20. Which therapy is designed to boost scalp cell turnover by removing dead skin layers?

A. LED therapy

B. Exfoliation

C. Steaming

D. Tension massage

title: Tricocare PH1 Exam Day 5-8
content:
Tricocare PH1 – Final Exam: Multiple Choice

 Which type of hair is most likely to experience shrinkage and requires more moisture retention strategies?

   A. Straight Asian hair

   B. Wavy European hair

   C. Tightly curled Afro hair

   D. Fine Caucasian hair



What kind of language should hair professionals use when discussing possible scalp issues?

   A. Diagnostic

   B. Medical

   C. Suggestive

   D. Observational



What is a common visible sign of high porosity hair?

   A. Hair that is slow to dry

   B. Hair that feels waxy when wet

   C. Hair that absorbs water quickly and dries fast

   D. Hair that retains styles for long periods



What is the main protein that makes up the hair shaft?

   A. Collagen

   B. Elastin

   C. Keratin

   D. Melanin



What role does the dermal papilla play in hair growth?

   A. Protects the cuticle

   B. Anchors the follicle

   C. Supplies nutrients to the hair bulb

   D. Produces sebum



Which term refers to compulsive hair pulling often related to stress or anxiety?

   A. Alopecia areata

   B. Folliculitis

   C. Trichotillomania

   D. Traction alopecia



Which phase of the hair cycle is the 'shedding' phase?

   A. Anagen

   B. Telogen

   C. Exogen

   D. Catagen



 Which statement about biotin is accurate?

   A. Everyone benefits from high biotin supplements

   B. Biotin directly prevents dandruff

   C. Biotin helps hair growth only if you're deficient

   D. Biotin replaces the need for protein

Which of these would be an ethical and appropriate statement from a stylist to a client?

   A. You have seborrheic dermatitis

   B. This looks like psoriasis

   C. Your scalp is very dry, I recommend seeing a specialist

   D. You should stop using your medication



Why is hydration important for healthy hair and scalp?

   A. It strengthens pigment cells

   B. It regulates melanin production

   C. It supports barrier function and elasticity

   D. It thickens the cuticle



Which of these is considered a tension zone where hair may thin due to tight styling?

   A. Crown

   B. Midshaft

   C. Ends

   D. Fringe



 Which scalp condition is characterised by greasy yellow flakes and redness?

   A. Psoriasis

   B. Eczema

   C. Seborrheic dermatitis

   D. Tinea capitis





 High-porosity hair is most commonly caused by which of the following?

   A. Excess sebum

   B. Product build-up

   C. Environmental exposure

   D. Chemical damage



 Which consultation technique encourages deeper, more personal responses?

   A. Closed questions

   B. Open questions

   C. Yes/no questions

   D. Leading questions



Why should scalp exfoliation treatments be avoided on certain clients?

   A. They can lighten the hair colour

   B. They increase dandruff

   C. They irritate broken or infected skin

   D. They increase oil production



Which hormone is associated with androgenic hair thinning in both men and women?

   A. Estrogen

   B. Cortisol

   C. DHT

   D. Insulin





Which ingredient is known to help exfoliate the scalp by breaking down dead skin cells?

   A. Caffeine

   B. Salicylic acid

   C. Vitamin D

   D. Castor oil



Which nutrient deficiency is most strongly linked to excessive hair shedding?

   A. Vitamin A

   B. Zinc

   C. Iron

   D. Biotin



Which growth pattern is commonly found at the crown of the head?

   A. Cowlick

   B. Fringe

   C. Recession zone

   D. Tension patch



Which layer of the scalp contains the hair follicle, blood vessels, and sebaceous glands?

   A. Epidermis

   B. Dermis

   C. Hypodermis

   D. Cuticle
